modules.title: Machine Learning Fundamentals
modules.description: Core ideas behind learning from data

steps.content: Machine learning lets computers learn patterns from data instead of following hand-written rules. The three main families are supervised learning (labeled examples), unsupervised learning (finding structure in unlabeled data), and reinforcement learning (learning from rewards).

Inputs to a model are called features and the thing we want to predict is the label. We train on one portion of the data and keep a separate test set to check how the model performs on examples it has never seen.

steps.question: Predicting the price of a house from its size and location is an example of:
steps.explanation: Predicting a continuous number is regression.

steps.question: The input variables fed to a model are called ______.
steps.explanation: Features are the measurable inputs; the label is the target.

steps.question: Order the typical machine learning workflow
steps.explanation: Data comes first, then training, then evaluation, then deployment.

steps.question: Why do we keep a separate test set?
options: To measure performance on unseen data
To increase the amount of training data
steps.explanation: A test set estimates how the model generalizes.

steps.content: Supervised learning learns from labeled examples. Classification predicts a category, such as spam or not spam. Regression predicts a number, such as a temperature.

Linear regression fits a straight line by minimizing the squared difference between predictions and true values. k-nearest neighbors classifies a point by looking at the labels of its closest training examples, and decision trees split the data using a series of questions.

steps.question: Which of these is a classification task?
options: Deciding whether an email is spam
steps.explanation: Spam detection outputs a category, so it is classification.

steps.question: Linear regression minimizes the squared ______ between predictions and true values.
steps.explanation: The fit that minimizes squared error is the least-squares line.

steps.question: Order these scikit-learn lines to train and use a model
steps.explanation: Import, create, fit on training data, then predict.

steps.question: With k = 3 in k-nearest neighbors, a new point is classified by:
options: The majority label among its 3 nearest neighbors
The label of the farthest neighbor
steps.explanation: k-NN votes among the k closest examples.

steps.content: Overfitting happens when a model memorizes the training data, noise included, and performs poorly on new data. Underfitting is the opposite: the model is too simple to capture the pattern.

Accuracy is the share of correct predictions. Precision asks how many predicted positives were truly positive, and recall asks how many true positives were found. Cross-validation repeats training and testing on different splits to get a more reliable estimate.

steps.question: A model scores 99% on training data but 60% on test data. What is the most likely problem?
steps.explanation: A large gap between training and test performance signals overfitting.

steps.question: Evaluating a model by rotating through several data splits is called cross-______.
steps.explanation: k-fold cross-validation averages results over k different splits.

steps.question: Order the steps of k-fold cross-validation
snippets: Repeat so every fold is used once
Split the data into k folds
steps.explanation: Each fold takes a turn as the validation set.

steps.question: Precision measures:
options: Of the predicted positives, how many are truly positive
Of the true positives, how many were found
The share of all correct predictions
The size of the training set

steps.content: Unsupervised learning finds structure in data that has no labels. Clustering groups similar items together, for example segmenting customers by their behavior.

k-means is a popular clustering method. You choose K, the number of clusters, and the algorithm repeatedly assigns points to the nearest centroid and recomputes the centroids. Dimensionality reduction methods such as PCA compress many features into a few while keeping most of the variation.

steps.question: In k-means, K is the number of ______ the algorithm looks for.
steps.explanation: You choose K, the number of clusters, before running the algorithm.

steps.question: Order the steps of the k-means algorithm
snippets: Assign each point to the nearest centroid
Recompute each centroid as its cluster mean
steps.explanation: Assign, update, and repeat until it converges.

steps.question: PCA is mainly used to:
options: Reduce the number of features while keeping most of the variance
steps.explanation: PCA projects data onto fewer dimensions that capture the most variance.
